title: Affine formal modules: Quotient
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring, I an ideal, B its I-adic completion, X=Spec A, and J the associated ideal sheaf. For each finite B-module N, the canonical sheaf quotient system formalCompletionFunctor J applied to tilde of N restricted to A is a coherent formal J-module. Explicitly, every level n+1 is coherent, annihilated by J^(n+1), and its successive reduction is the quotient by J^(n+1), with the given projection equation. Thus the already constructed quotient-system functor lifts to the full subcategory of coherent formal systems; call this actual lifted functor Q. This is a construction from the fixed quotient functor, not an unspecified choice of an equivalence.

proof.text: Let B be the I-adic completion. Prove the local helper finite_of_completion_generators: an A-linear surjective map q from a finite B-module to P, satisfying q(a x)=0 for a in I^k, makes P finite over A. Choose finite B-generators s. Every b in B has the same image modulo I^k as of(a) for some a in A, by surjectivity of the quotient projection. AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval puts b-of(a) in I^k B. Induction over ideal products shows q((b-of(a))x)=0. Induction on the B-span of s now places q(x) in the A-span of q(s), which is therefore all of P.

For the tilde sheaf F of N restricted to A, the ideal-times theorem makes every positive ideal power quasi-coherent. Reuse idealModuleProduct_quasicoherent from CoherentFormalModule (accessible by import all), and quasi-coherent cokernel closure, to make Q_n=F/J^(n+1)F quasi-coherent. The affine cokernel-image theorem makes its top quotient projection surjective. Compose this with tilde.isoTop to get an A-linear surjection q:N to Gamma(Q_n). The ideal-times theorem identifies the affine section range of the power inclusion with J(top)^(n+1). By hJ and ideal_top_ofIdealTop, this contains the image of each a in I^(n+1). Reuse idealModuleProduct_quotient_zero to show multiplication by the power on its quotient is zero. Evaluating multiplication on a pure tensor proves q(a x)=0. Apply step 1 to obtain finite top sections; extending scalars from A to Gamma(Spec A) preserves finiteness. The affine finite-type criterion on the one-open top cover and the locally Noetherian coherence criterion give coherence of every Q_n.

Reuse the existing idealModuleProduct_quotient_zero and formalModuleQuotient_iterated theorems from CoherentFormalModule, accessible by the proof-only import all. The first gives annihilation of each quotient by its defining ideal power. Specialize the second to upper exponent n+2 and lower exponent n+1; its projection equation is definitionally the formalCompletionSystem transition. Combine coherence from step 2, annihilation, and this quotient isomorphism to establish IsCoherentFormalModule. The unchanged ObjectProperty.lift definition then gives Q. No categorical helper is reproved.

theorem coherentFormalModules_affine_quotient_coherent
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (J : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom))
    (N : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N)) :
    IsCoherentFormalModule J ((ObjectProperty.ι
        (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N) ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A)) ⋙
      tilde.functor (CommRingCat.of A) ⋙ formalCompletionFunctor J).obj N)
